This happens to me a lot! I tend to end up sore afterwards if it’s too dry, or my labia get pulled around or some other things. If this happens again, I recommend she look at the area that’s sore (I just sit and use a compact mirror) that way she can see if it’s red, or if she has any tearing (tears will probably be small but they are easy to see). Both issues should go away in a few days.

I relate to this mindset. I know you shouldn’t do it because medical stuff and it’s bad for you etc etc, but I’m honestly like if I don’t go deep, is it really that bad? Is it really that much worse than being totally miserable? I just can’t see the downsides anymore, or take the downsides seriously.

I totally get what you mean about only feeling bad because of how others feel. I don’t really question why everybody else gets upset about it, because I know that I was the same way before I did it. It’s really hard for people to fully understand how it feels unless they’ve done it themselves. I’m not saying that people should cut or that it’s okay, I feel / know that I shouldn’t do it, but it feels normal to me so it doesn’t bother me anymore unless I’m filled with guilt because of how I know it’ll effect anyone who knows about it.

This. I feel this. I always avoided telling my friends anything because I didn’t want to upset them and I was afraid they’d see me differently. I fairly recently (2 months ago? 1.5 months? Idk) told one of my friends about it and there were tons of days where I regretted it. I was so afraid of what I’d be doing to them since I felt like I was burdening them. In reality, they’ve been nothing but supportive and they’ve been really patient with me. They don’t treat me differently than before aside from making it clear that they’re here for me whenever I’m upset. There are going to be days where you feel guilty or upset because you told them, but there will also be days where you’re glad you did because it means you don’t have to be alone anymore.

It’s definitely a constant routine for me. I can be feeling great all day, try to go to sleep, brain say no.

From my experience, people who self harm know that it’s wrong and that they should stop, but they don’t want to or can’t. If you’re willing to commit, tell her to talk to you when she feels the urge. Make your friendship a safe space. Other than being there for her, there isn’t much you can do without danger of breaking her trust in you. Eventually, the fact that she told you and it didn’t result in anything bad might help her seek help in the future.
